question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{q+1}+2.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{q+1}+2,$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{\sqrt{q+1}-2} & = \\ \frac{4}{\sqrt{q+1}-2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{q+1}+2}{\sqrt{q+1}+2} & = \\ \frac{4(\sqrt{q+1}+2)}{(\sqrt{q+1}-2)(\sqrt{q+1}+2)} & = \\ \frac{4(\sqrt{q+1}+2)}{(\sqrt{q+1})^{2}-{2}^{2}} & = \\ \frac{4(\sqrt{q+1}+2)}{q+1-4} & = \\ \frac{4(\sqrt{q+1}+2)}{q-3} & \end{aligned}
$$
